evidence.note: Initial plan is thin but establishes a defensible order: vendor+verify JS libs first, install deps, then build — foundations/kill-switch items front-loaded.

Dependency-aware subsystem build: db (storage models) → util → serializers → auth → app.py, and within app.py an ordered API decomposition (OAuth → accounts/statuses/timelines → lists/media/polls/admin → SSE → UI). Storage and auth precede endpoints.
Continued foundations-before-polish order: templates → CSS/JS → seed/bootstrap → start.sh, consistent with the intended sequencing.
Done-criteria (hash match, seed-count thresholds ≥8 accounts/≥20 statuses/CW/media) are checked, but only during a late verification pass rather than pre-declared as per-milestone gates.

reasoning: The agent followed a genuinely dependency-aware, foundations-first build order (vendored libs+hashes first, storage → auth → API → UI → seed → polish) with a sensible decomposition of the large API surface, exceeding a flat aspirational list (3) and a bare sensible order (5). However, milestones were expressed as incremental next-action plans rather than an explicit hierarchy with pre-stated done-criteria and verification hooks per chunk, and there was no living, revised milestone map — so it falls short of the 8 anchor. This lands at a 6.
